sections.heading: Reflexive verbs
sections.body: Some verbs describe something you do to yourself: *levantarse* (to get up), *ducharse* (to shower), *vestirse* (to get dressed). In the dictionary they end in *-se*. When you conjugate them, a reflexive pronoun goes before the verb.

sections.heading: You already know one
sections.body:
*Me llamo Ana* is a reflexive verb: *llamarse*, "to call oneself". The same pattern: *te llamas, se llama, nos llamamos, se llaman*.

Negatives put *no* before the pronoun: *No me levanto temprano.* (I don't get up early.) With an infinitive, the pronoun can attach to the end: *Necesito ducharme.* (I need to shower.)

sections.heading: Talking about your day
sections.body:
Useful sequence words: *primero* (first), *después* (then, afterwards), *luego* (then, later), *por último* (finally). Also: *temprano* (early), *tarde* (late), *todos los días* (every day).

Not every daily-routine verb is reflexive: *desayunar* (to have breakfast), *almorzar* (to have lunch), *cenar* (to have dinner) are regular verbs. *Acostarse* (to go to bed) and *vestirse* (to get dressed) change their stem in some forms — *me acuesto, me visto* — you'll learn the full pattern in the next lesson.

examples: Primero me ducho y después desayuno.
First I shower and then I have breakfast.
What time do you get up?
We go to bed at eleven.
Ellos se duchan por la noche.
Me visto y luego me peino.
I get dressed and then I comb my hair.
No me levanto temprano los domingos.
I don't get up early on Sundays.
Ceno con mi familia todos los días.
I have dinner with my family every day.
Mi madre se despierta a las seis.
My mother wakes up at six.
Ustedes se bañan por la mañana.
You all bathe in the morning.
Our names are Ana and Luis.
I have coffee and bread for breakfast.
